title: Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

reports.title: Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant admits to improper use of Flock cameras per docs
Critics warned about Flock surveillance. Three Houston-area investigations are fueling those concerns.

summary:
A Fort Bend County Sheriff's Office lieutenant used Flock camera records to look up one license plate 41 times and another 148 times between January 2022 and December 2025. The lieutenant admitted those searches were not for official law enforcement work. A resident filed a complaint saying the lieutenant was stalking them and that they feared for their family's safety. An internal affairs investigation found the lieutenant violated department rules and suspended the lieutenant for two days.

The lieutenant said the searches came from concern that the two drivers were lurking near the lieutenant's home and family, and documents describe a contentious family relationship with one vehicle owner. The lieutenant is not named because there are no criminal charges. A law professor said this kind of improper access is usually an administrative or ethical violation unless there is clear intent to harm. The lieutenant said the information was not used or shared. ABC13 is awaiting responses from the lieutenant and the sheriff's office.
